lessons.title: Join Tables
lessons.summary: Combine related rows from multiple tables.
lessons.explanation: JOIN connects rows through matching key columns, such as employees.department_id and departments.id.

exercises.prompt: List each employee with their department name. Return columns: first_name, last_name, department. Order by: e.id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, d.name AS department FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id ORDER BY e.id;

exercises.prompt: Show each project assignment with employee name and project name. Return columns: first_name, last_name, project. Order by: e.id ASC, p.id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, p.name AS project FROM employee_projects ep JOIN employees e ON e.id = ep.employee_id JOIN projects p ON p.id = ep.project_id ORDER BY e.id, p.id;

exercises.prompt: List orders with the customer name and order status. Return columns: id, customer, status. Order by: o.id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT o.id, c.name AS customer, o.status FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id ORDER BY o.id;

exercises.prompt: Show each sale with its order date. Return columns: product, quantity, unit_price, order_date. Order by: s.id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT s.product, s.quantity, s.unit_price, o.order_date FROM sales s JOIN orders o ON o.id = s.order_id ORDER BY s.id;

exercises.prompt: List employees assigned to the Analytics Portal project. Return columns: first_name, last_name. Order by: e.id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name FROM employee_projects ep JOIN employees e ON e.id = ep.employee_id JOIN projects p ON p.id = ep.project_id WHERE p.name = 'Analytics Portal' ORDER BY e.id;

lessons.title: Aggregate With GROUP BY
lessons.explanation: GROUP BY creates one result row for each group, and aggregate functions calculate values per group.

exercises.prompt: Calculate total sales revenue per category. Return columns: category, revenue. Order by: category ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT category, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS revenue FROM sales GROUP BY category ORDER BY category;

exercises.prompt: Count employees in each department. Return columns: department, employee_count. Order by: d.name ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT d.name AS department, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.name ORDER BY d.name;

exercises.prompt: Calculate the average salary for each role. Return columns: role, average_salary. Order by: role ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT role, AVG(salary) AS average_salary FROM employees GROUP BY role ORDER BY role;

exercises.prompt: Count orders by status. Return columns: status, order_count. Order by: status ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY status ORDER BY status;

exercises.prompt: Calculate total project hours per project. Return columns: name, total_hours. Order by: p.name ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT p.name, SUM(ep.hours_per_week) AS total_hours FROM employee_projects ep JOIN projects p ON p.id = ep.project_id GROUP BY p.name ORDER BY p.name;

lessons.title: Filter Groups With HAVING
lessons.explanation: WHERE filters rows before grouping. HAVING filters grouped results after aggregate values are calculated.
lessons.example:
SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM orders
GROUP BY status
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

exercises.prompt: Find categories with total revenue above 1000. Return columns: category, revenue. Order by: category ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT category, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS revenue FROM sales GROUP BY category HAVING SUM(quantity * unit_price) > 1000 ORDER BY category;

exercises.prompt: Find departments with more than one employee. Return columns: department, employee_count. Order by: d.name ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT d.name AS department, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.name HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY d.name;

exercises.prompt: Find order statuses used more than once. Return columns: status, order_count. Order by: status ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY status HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY status;

exercises.prompt: Find projects with at least 20 assigned hours per week. Return columns: name, total_hours. Order by: p.name ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT p.name, SUM(ep.hours_per_week) AS total_hours FROM employee_projects ep JOIN projects p ON p.id = ep.project_id GROUP BY p.name HAVING SUM(ep.hours_per_week) >= 20 ORDER BY p.name;

exercises.prompt: Find customer segments with at least 2 customers. Return columns: segment, customer_count. Order by: segment ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT segment, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY segment HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY segment;
